Romance & Dating Scams UK: Apps, Fake Profiles & Money

Romance scams on Tinder, Bumble, Hinge and Facebook Dating. How verification badges are faked, when the conversation moves to investing, and how to report it.

Romance fraud is patient. The opening is a normal match; the money comes weeks or months later, once the relationship feels real. That delay is the point — by the time a request arrives, refusing it feels like doubting someone you care about.

Two signals matter more than any profile detail: being moved off the app to a private messenger, and any reason you cannot meet or video-call. Neither proves fraud on its own, but together they precede almost every case in this section.

The apps, and what changes between them

The pattern is shared, the mechanics are not. Tinder and Bumble both run photo verification, and a message telling you to 'get verified first' through a link is a con rather than a platform feature. Hinge profiles carry prompts and answers, which gives an approach more material to mirror back at you. Facebook Dating sits inside an account that may already carry years of real-looking history.

When the conversation turns to money

Requests rarely arrive as requests. They arrive as an emergency, an opportunity, or a test of trust. The investment version — a trading app or crypto platform introduced by someone you have been talking to for weeks — is covered in our relationship investment scam guide, and INTERPOL now discourages the older 'pig butchering' label because it describes victims in terms of livestock.

The impersonation version borrows a role that explains why meeting is impossible: our military romance scam guide covers deployment stories, and the fees that follow them for leave, transport or medical costs.

What a verification badge does and does not prove

Photo verification checks that the person in the photos is the person holding the phone. It does not check who they are, where they are, or whether anything they have told you is true. A verified profile can still be run by someone using their own face and a false name.

Treat a badge as evidence about photos, not about identity. The checks that actually help are a live video call you propose at short notice, and a reverse image search on the pictures.

How to check safely, without accusing anyone

Suggest a video call at a time you choose rather than one arranged days ahead. Keep the conversation inside the app until you have had one — moving to a private messenger removes the platform's ability to see reports or act on them.

Search a few phrases from the profile. Reused biographies are common, because the same text is worked across many accounts at once.

Do not send money, gift cards or crypto to someone you have not met, and do not receive and forward money on anyone's behalf, which can make you a money mule regardless of intent.

If you have already sent money

Contact your bank straight away and say the payment may be authorised push payment fraud. UK reimbursement rules apply to many cases, and an eligible claim is normally decided within five business days, with a maximum 35-business-day stop-clock while a firm investigates.

Keep the profile, the chat and the payment references before you block anyone — screenshots first, then report and block. Expect a second approach later offering to recover the money for a fee; that is a separate scam.

How to report a romance scam in the UK

Report the profile inside the app so the platform can act on the account, then report the fraud to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland.

Forward scam texts free to 7726 and suspicious emails to report@phishing.gov.uk.

Common questions

Does a verified badge mean the person is genuine?

No. Photo verification confirms the person in the pictures is holding the phone. It says nothing about their name, location or intentions, and a verified account can still be operated under a false identity.

They will video call but only ever briefly, or the camera fails. Is that a red flag?

It is a reason to keep checking rather than a conclusion. Repeated technical failures around calls, especially when paired with pressure about money, are common in these cases. Propose a call at a time you choose and see what happens.

Can I get money back after a romance scam?

Often, but not always. Tell your bank it may be authorised push payment fraud. Eligible claims are normally decided within five business days, with a maximum 35-business-day stop-clock. Reimbursement can be refused where a customer acted with gross negligence.

Someone has offered to recover money I lost. Should I use them?

Treat it as a second scam until proven otherwise. Recovery approaches target people already known to have lost money, and legitimate recovery does not require an up-front fee to a cold caller.
